_meta.note: Curated detection guidance for the most-tested ATT&CK techniques. Best-effort, not authoritative — always cross-reference attack.mitre.org and tune for your environment.

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — powershell.exe / pwsh.exe process creation (note parent / cmdline)
Sysmon EID 7 — System.Management.Automation.dll loaded by non-PS host (suspicious)
Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational EID 4104 — Script Block Logging
Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational EID 4103 — Module Logging
Security EID 4688 — process creation w/ PSReadline / encoded commands
AMSI / Defender ETW for in-memory script content

fp_notes: Admin scripts and SCCM run PowerShell at scale — pivot on parent (excel.exe / outlook.exe / wscript.exe = high signal)
Encoded commands (-EncodedCommand) are common in SCCM but rare in human admin use

T1059.003.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — cmd.exe with suspicious parent (winword.exe / outlook.exe / regsvr32.exe)
Security EID 4688 — process creation

fp_notes: cmd.exe is everywhere — selectivity comes from parent + cmdline patterns

T1059.004.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

linux: auditd execve syscalls for /bin/sh, /bin/bash with notable comm
EDR shell history exfil / large pipe-to-shell patterns
macos: ESF NOTIFY_EXEC events with unusual parent (e.g., browser, document app)

fp_notes: Build pipelines and admin scripts produce massive shell volume — filter on user / TTY / parent

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task

windows: Security EID 4698 — A scheduled task was created (target name + author)
Security EID 4702 — A scheduled task was updated
Security EID 4699 — A scheduled task was deleted
Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational EID 106
Sysmon EID 1 — schtasks.exe / taskeng.exe process creation
Sysmon EID 11 — file creation under \Windows\System32\Tasks\

fp_notes: Software updaters (Adobe, Chrome, Edge, NVIDIA) churn maintenance tasks constantly
Domain admins deploy tasks via GPO — pivot on author / source IP

T1053.003.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron

linux: Sysmon for Linux — file create/modify events under cron paths
Process events for crontab edits via crontab -e
macos: Same cron paths as Linux; LaunchAgents covered under T1543.001/004

fp_notes: Package installs add cron entries — correlate with package manager activity

T1547.001.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

windows: Sysmon EID 13 — registry value set under HKLM/HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run* / RunOnce*
Security EID 4657 — registry value modified (requires SACL)
Sysmon EID 11 — file create in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\

fp_notes: Most software installs write Run keys — pivot on uncommon binaries and untrusted paths (%APPDATA%, %TEMP%)

T1547.004.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Winlogon Helper DLL

windows: Sysmon EID 13 — registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\(Userinit|Shell|Notify)
Sysmon EID 7 — image load by winlogon.exe of an unusual DLL

fp_notes: Userinit/Shell modifications are extremely rare on healthy hosts — high-fidelity signal

T1543.003.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

windows: Security EID 4697 — A service was installed
System EID 7045 — A service was installed in the system
Sysmon EID 1 — sc.exe / New-Service process creation
Sysmon EID 13 — registry writes under HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\*

fp_notes: Software installers create services — selectivity from service binary path and account
PsExec and remote management create transient services (PSEXESVC, etc.)

T1543.001.name: Create or Modify System Process: Launch Agent
fp_notes: Most apps install LaunchAgents on first run — selectivity from signing / unsigned binaries

T1548.002.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — process integrity High/System with parent of Medium and IntegrityLevel mismatch
Sysmon EID 13 — registry writes to HKCU\Software\Classes\* (CMSTP / fodhelper / eventvwr UAC bypass families)
Defender ETW — UAC bypass detections

fp_notes: Fodhelper / sdclt / eventvwr-based UAC bypasses are well-known — high-fidelity rules exist (sigma)
Legitimate consent prompts on admin workstations — filter via session

T1003.001.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory

windows: Sysmon EID 10 — process accessed lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1010 / 0x1410 / 0x1438 / 0x143A
Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing EID 4663 — handle to lsass with sensitive access (requires SACL)
Microsoft Defender — Sensitive Credential Memory Read
EDR LSASS protection tampering events

fp_notes: Antivirus / EDR processes access lsass legitimately — allowlist by signed process
Mimikatz / pypykatz / nanodump / dumpert are common families — process command-line filters help

T1003.002.name: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — reg.exe save HKLM\SAM / vssadmin create shadow / esentutl with copy
Sysmon EID 11 — file create matching SAM/SYSTEM hive copies in non-standard paths
Security EID 4688 — process creation w/ above signatures

fp_notes: Backup software interacts with VSS — filter on parent / signed status

T1110.003.name: Brute Force: Password Spraying

windows: Security EID 4625 — failed logons grouped by source / single-account-many-IPs or one-IP-many-accounts
Security EID 4624 — successful logons after sequence of 4625 from same source
office-365: AzureAD Sign-in logs — UserPrincipalName + IPAddress + ResultType
UAL UserLoggedIn / UserLoginFailed grouped by IP

fp_notes: Misconfigured services can trigger massive 4625 — exclude known bad-credential service accounts

T1078.name: Valid Accounts

windows: Security EID 4624 — Type 3/10 (network/RDP) from unusual source
Security EID 4672 — Special privileges assigned
office-365: Sign-in logs with unusual UserAgent / DeviceTrust state

fp_notes: Always-on VPN exits and mobile roaming generate noisy 'unusual location' alerts

T1018.name: Remote System Discovery

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — net.exe view, nltest, dsquery, Get-ADComputer
Sysmon EID 3 — large fan-out SMB/445 from a single source

fp_notes: Domain admin scripts inventory hosts at scale — filter by source host class

T1057.name: Process Discovery

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — tasklist / Get-Process / wmic process list / qprocess
Sysmon EID 10 — handles opened to many processes from a single source
linux: auditd execve for ps, top, htop, lsof
macos: ESF NOTIFY_EXEC for ps, top, lsof

fp_notes: Monitoring agents enumerate processes constantly — exclude known agents

T1082.name: System Information Discovery

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — systeminfo.exe / hostname.exe / wmic computersystem / Get-ComputerInfo
Security EID 4688 — process creation matching above
linux: auditd execve uname, hostnamectl, lscpu, /etc/os-release reads

fp_notes: Asset inventory scans run these constantly — pivot on chained discovery (multiple recon cmds in 60s)

T1083.name: File and Directory Discovery

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — dir, tree, where, Get-ChildItem -Recurse with broad patterns
Sysmon EID 11 (read access logs require Win 10+ + audit policy)
linux: auditd execve for find / locate / ls -laR with notable args

fp_notes: Backup and AV scanning generate huge volume — filter by parent and recursion depth heuristics

T1027.name: Obfuscated Files or Information

windows: PowerShell EID 4104 — script blocks with high entropy / IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString patterns
Sysmon EID 1 — powershell -EncodedCommand … with base64 payloads
AMSI flagged content

fp_notes: SCCM / Intune use encoded commands — allowlist by known publisher cert

T1070.001.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs

windows: Security EID 1102 — Audit log was cleared
System EID 104 — Log was cleared
Sysmon EID 1 — wevtutil cl, Clear-EventLog

fp_notes: Log clearance is rare and high-fidelity — almost always investigate

T1112.name: Modify Registry

windows: Sysmon EID 12/13/14 — registry create/set/delete with key + value detail
Security EID 4657 — registry value modified (requires SACL)

fp_notes: Massive baseline volume — selectivity from key path patterns

T1105.name: Ingress Tool Transfer

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — curl.exe / certutil.exe -urlcache / bitsadmin / Invoke-WebRequest / wget.exe
Sysmon EID 3 — outbound from unusual processes (lolbins) to unusual destinations
Sysmon EID 11 — file create in %TEMP% / %APPDATA% post-download
Proxy / DNS logs — uncommon destinations from server hosts
linux: auditd / Sysmon for Linux execve for wget/curl with output redirect to disk

fp_notes: Software updaters use BITS legitimately — filter by destination domain reputation

T1071.001.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols

windows: Sysmon EID 3 — outbound from unusual binaries (lolbins) on 80/443
Proxy logs — unusual UA strings, beaconing intervals
DNS logs — high-entropy / DGA domains

fp_notes: Beaconing detection benefits from interval-and-jitter analysis, not just IOCs

T1090.name: Proxy

windows: Sysmon EID 3 — sustained outbound TCP from unusual processes
Firewall / NetFlow — long-lived flows to new external endpoints

fp_notes: Legit reverse-tunnels (ngrok, cloudflared) increasingly common — score by binary reputation

T1486.name: Data Encrypted for Impact

windows: Sysmon EID 11 — bursts of writes with new extensions / ransom notes
Sysmon EID 23 — file delete bursts (shadow copy / recycle bin clear)
Defender ASR — ransomware-like behavior detections

fp_notes: Detection at write-burst level is late — pair with EDR behavioral protection

T1489.name: Service Stop

windows: System EID 7036 — service entered the stopped state (filter on EDR / AV / backup services)
Security EID 4697 — service installed (precursor)
Sysmon EID 1 — sc.exe stop / Stop-Service / net stop

fp_notes: Patching reboots stop services normally — pivot on user / non-admin originator

T1485.name: Data Destruction

windows: Sysmon EID 23/26 — file delete bursts
Sysmon EID 1 — sdelete, cipher /w, format, fsutil file setzerodata

fp_notes: Disposal / re-imaging tools trigger this — pivot on session and host context

T1490.name: Inhibit System Recovery

windows: Sysmon EID 1 — vssadmin delete shadows / wmic shadowcopy delete / wbadmin delete catalog / bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures
System EID 7036 — VSS service stopped

fp_notes: Very high-fidelity — VSS deletion is rare in normal ops

T1136.001.name: Create Account: Local Account

windows: Security EID 4720 — A user account was created
Security EID 4732 — A member was added to a security-enabled local group
Sysmon EID 1 — net.exe user /add

fp_notes: Onboarding scripts create accounts at scale — filter by source / time of day

T1021.002.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

windows: Security EID 4624 type 3 from non-DC source
Sysmon EID 3 — outbound 445 from non-server hosts
Sysmon EID 11 — file create in ADMIN$ / C$ from remote source

fp_notes: Admin tooling (PsExec, SCCM remote actions) exercises this constantly

T1021.001.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol

windows: Security EID 4624 type 10 (RDP)
Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational EID 21/25
Firewall — inbound 3389 from outside known jumpbox subnets

fp_notes: RDP from outside jumpbox = always investigate; inside jumpbox = baseline noise

T1133.name: External Remote Services

office-365: AzureAD sign-ins — VPN gateways, Citrix, AnyConnect, GlobalProtect appliances

fp_notes: VPN and remote-work tooling is heavy baseline — focus on impossible travel + new device

T1567.002.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage

windows: Proxy / DLP logs — POST/PUT to *.dropbox / mega.nz / *.s3.amazonaws / *.transfer.sh / paste.ee
Sysmon EID 3 — outbound from unusual processes to known file-share CIDRs

fp_notes: SaaS productivity tools generate massive cloud-storage traffic — DLP-content rules > IP-only rules

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel

windows: NetFlow — long-lived high-volume out-bytes from a host with low in-bytes ratio
Proxy — POST traffic with unusually large payloads

fp_notes: Backup uploads + cloud sync produce similar shapes — bias on host class and process
